LanguageData.RHAH_History_A001_FleeingTenantFarmer.de: [PAWN_nameDef] worked the family's rented fields for ratkin nobles. After rent, there was barely enough grain to keep the household half-fed. When war reached the fields, neither the tenancy rolls nor the land offered any protection, and [PAWN_pronoun] left the ancestral plots with the refugees.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A002_DroughtFieldWatcher.de: [PAWN_nameDef] tended the last dry plots at home, but year after year the rains failed and the seedlings shriveled in the sun. The landlord still demanded seed grain. In the end, [PAWN_pronoun] left with the other tenants and their empty sacks; there was nothing left to tend.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A003_ScavengerOfFallowField: [PAWN_nameDef]'s household ran out of food before the grain collectors even arrived, and the fields had gone to weeds. Gleaning at night meant being chased by rats and grain patrols. When [PAWN_pronoun] left home, only a few salvaged seeds remained.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A004_FamineHerdTender.title: famine herder
herder
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A004_FamineHerdTender.descr: [PAWN_nameDef] tended livestock for a ranch. During the famine, the owner sold some animals and surrendered most of the rest for army rations. With the pens empty, [PAWN_pronoun] led the few survivors out with the refugees in search of grazing.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A005_DroughtWellWaterCarrie: [PAWN_nameDef] hauled water from the village well in exchange for grain. By late summer the well was down to mud, and each day brought a longer walk for water. After the villages fought over the remaining source, [PAWN_pronoun] left the old well with empty buckets and the water crew.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A006_GranaryBookkeeper.desc: [PAWN_nameDef] kept the granary books and found far more sacks listed than actually stored. The steward planned to blame [PAWN_objective] for the shortage. Before the inquiry, [PAWN_pronoun] fled with the list.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A007_MoldyGrainSifter.title: moldy grain sifter
sifter
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A007_MoldyGrainSifter.descr: [PAWN_nameDef] sifted grain at a mill, where spoiled grain that should have been discarded was mixed into famine rations. After seeing children receive it, [PAWN_pronoun] refused to keep quiet. That cost [PAWN_objective] both the job and the lodging, and [PAWN_pronoun] left with those fleeing town.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A008_OrphanedMillhand.title: abandoned mill worker
mill worker
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A008_OrphanedMillhand.descr: [PAWN_nameDef] worked at a mill whose owner fled one night over grain debts, leaving a failing millstone and unpaid wages. When the owner did not return, [PAWN_pronoun] salvaged the usable tools and sought work in another camp.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A009_GranaryCarpenter.title: granary carpenter
carpenter
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A009_GranaryCarpenter.descr: [PAWN_nameDef] repaired the village granary, whose walls had been hollowed out by rats. Lumber for repairs went to the landlord's own roof instead. When heavy rain brought the granary down, the workers lost their shed too, and [PAWN_pronoun] left the village with them.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A010_RagStitcher.title: old clothes mender
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A010_RagStitcher.descriptio: After the weaving shop closed and the cloth was requisitioned, [PAWN_nameDef] mended old clothes for grain. Poor customers had no new fabric, only garments to take apart and sew again. When a fire destroyed the remaining cloth and the lodging, [PAWN_pronoun] packed up the needles and thread and left with the refugees.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A011_DiseasedHideTanner.des: [PAWN_nameDef] tanned hides for a hunting estate until the nobles closed the hills and the steady supply stopped. That winter, even hides from diseased livestock had to be traded for grain. When that work dried up too, [PAWN_pronoun] left with a caravan.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A012_HerbSorter.title: replacement herbalist
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A012_HerbSorter.description: [PAWN_nameDef] had only been an herb gatherer's assistant. When plague killed the village herbalist, all that remained were incomplete notes. To treat the family's fevers, [PAWN_pronoun] took over the medicine basket and the quarantine work, but was driven out when the shed closed.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A013_KilnWatcher.title: displaced kiln worker
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A013_KilnWatcher.descriptio: [PAWN_nameDef] tended a landlord's brick kiln all winter and still could not obtain enough fuel or a place to stay. When the kiln went cold, [PAWN_pronoun] left with hands damaged by the smoke and sought repair work at shelters.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A014_NightFamineEscapee.des: After years of failed harvests, the village's last sack of grain went to the elderly and the children, leaving [PAWN_nameDef] without food. On the night people began barring doors and seizing grain, [PAWN_pronoun] took an old waterskin and slipped away.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A015_RiverbankBridgeBuilder: [PAWN_nameDef] repaired boats by the river. When a flood broke the wooden bridge and stranded refugees on the bank, [PAWN_pronoun] built a makeshift bridge so the family could cross. By the time the water receded, the home village was empty.
[PAWN_nameDef] repeatedly returned to a looted village for pots, cloth, and seeds still fit to sow. Patrols eventually blocked the old road, cutting off even those scraps. Only then did [PAWN_pronoun] leave with the other refugees.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A017_SnowpathGuide.title: snow road guide
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A017_SnowpathGuide.descript: [PAWN_nameDef] guided caravans until early winter snow closed the mountain road and left a refugee party lost in the snow. Unable even to find the way home, [PAWN_pronoun] led them across the wilderness by footprints and wind direction.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A018_DustwayPorter.title: dryland porter
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A018_DustwayPorter.descript: [PAWN_nameDef] hauled cargo for a caravan crossing dry country when thieves took the waterskins and pack animals began collapsing. To recover withheld wages, [PAWN_pronoun] also took on the pack train. When the caravan broke up, [PAWN_pronoun] kept walking with the remaining animals.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A019_CampNightWatch.title: camp night guard
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A019_CampNightWatch.descrip: After several nights of grain raids at the camp where [PAWN_nameDef] was staying, the guards fled with their weapons. [PAWN_pronoun] took over the night watch and message runs. When the camp moved, [PAWN_pronoun] kept listening for trouble at night in the new group.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A020_LostAtTheCheckpoint.de: [PAWN_nameDef] traveled with family past grain-tax checkpoints, where refugees without papers could be detained. A failed detour separated them. [PAWN_pronoun] learned the patrol hours, but had to walk the rest of the road alone.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A021_OldMapmaker.title: waystation mapmaker
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A021_OldMapmaker.descriptio: [PAWN_nameDef] drew routes for a waystation until a warehouse fire destroyed the old maps. With only broken signposts left for refugees to follow, [PAWN_pronoun] sketched remembered roads on scraps of cloth and was chosen to guide them. There was no route home afterward.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A022_KinSeekingExile.title: kin-seeking refugee
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A022_KinSeekingExile.descri: [PAWN_nameDef] was separated from family when refugees were forcibly divided between groups, and rain ruined the temporary registers. [PAWN_pronoun] asked for their names at campfires along the road. No relatives were found, so the search continued with the moving camps.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A023_RefugeeConvoyGuide.des: [PAWN_nameDef] had never been a leader. When a grain fight killed the old guide and left the group without directions to the next water source, the others put [PAWN_objective] in charge of routes and rations. Even after the group broke up, [PAWN_pronoun] led those still willing to follow.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A024_ShackRepairer.title: ruined house mender
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A024_ShackRepairer.descript: Rats chewed through the walls of [PAWN_nameDef]'s home, and a storm brought down the beams. Usable timber had been requisitioned for a granary. [PAWN_pronoun] repaired ruined houses for grain until that no longer paid, then left with refugees to find another roof.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A025_DisasterBurier.title: famine gravedigger
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A025_DisasterBurier.descrip: [PAWN_nameDef] buried the dead along village roads devastated by famine, where diseased and unclaimed bodies lay in numbers that frightened everyone away. The settlement then expelled [PAWN_objective] for contact with disease. Among the refugees, someone still had to do the same dirty work.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A026_GrainPetitionSpeaker.d: [PAWN_nameDef] petitioned the granary for the village's allotted rations, but every negotiation required another passage fee. When the village refused to pay, its grain was cut off. [PAWN_pronoun] took the register and empty bowls to unfamiliar settlements and begged from door to door.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A027_ReliefGoodsBroker.desc: [PAWN_nameDef] brokered exchanges at the market until soaring grain prices made every valuation unreliable overnight. To obtain medicine and seed for the family, [PAWN_pronoun] traveled with one refugee group after another, eventually losing [PAWN_possessive] own market stall.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A028_EscapedLedgerCopyist.d: [PAWN_nameDef] copied household registers and grain ledgers, saving only a few pages when the records building burned. On the road, [PAWN_pronoun] continued recording names and grain debts for people without papers. Every settlement treated [PAWN_objective] as a suspicious outsider.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A029_ReliefCook.title: replacement cook
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A029_ReliefCook.description: [PAWN_nameDef] did odd jobs in a public kitchen until plague killed the cook and no one dared distribute the remaining grain. [PAWN_pronoun] took over the stove so the children could eat first. When the kitchen closed, [PAWN_pronoun] left with the refugees.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A030_InfirmaryCaretaker.des: [PAWN_nameDef] had cared only for sick relatives until a granary fight filled the camp with wounded people. With doctors and medicine scarce, [PAWN_pronoun] learned to clean wounds and change dressings. When the camp was dispersed, [PAWN_pronoun] left with that incomplete training.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A031_RatEggCaretaker.title: caretaker of young ratkin
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A031_RatEggCaretaker.descri: [PAWN_nameDef] took turns carrying children in a refugee column until [PAWN_possessive] own relatives fell sick beside the road. When the column abandoned the sick and the young, [PAWN_pronoun] left with the young ratkin who could still walk. Promises that the adults would return became hard to trust.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A032_NightStoryteller.title: camp storyteller
storyteller
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A032_NightStoryteller.descr: [PAWN_nameDef] spun thread and knew old stories, while hunger and alarms kept the camp's children awake all night. On the dark roads between camps, [PAWN_pronoun] told stories to keep them walking steadily, and stayed with the refugee column.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A033_SealedVillageMessenger: [PAWN_nameDef] carried letters for the family in exchange for grain. Once several villages were sealed off, messengers on foot became the only way to pass news. When a patrol blocked the way home, [PAWN_pronoun] could not return and kept carrying letters for other camps.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A034_MarketSackPorter.title: market porter
porter
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A034_MarketSackPorter.descr: [PAWN_nameDef] hauled cargo at a market until it closed, taking both employer and wages with it. [PAWN_pronoun] moved the grain sacks into a temporary camp to keep them out of the looting. When the cargo owner fled that night, [PAWN_pronoun] moved on with the refugees left behind.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A035_UsedGoodsAppraiser.des: [PAWN_nameDef] appraised old pots and tools to trade for the family's rations. During the famine, people would accept only grain. After a few exchanges, robbers took the last possessions, and [PAWN_pronoun] left empty-handed with nothing left to value.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A036_RationMediator.title: ration mediator
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A036_RationMediator.descrip: [PAWN_nameDef] had settled irrigation disputes in the village, so two refugee groups chose [PAWN_objective] to mediate a fight over grain. The argument outside the granary still got out of hand. [PAWN_pronoun] left with the few willing to listen and sought another place to go.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A037_RationTicketKeeper.des: [PAWN_nameDef] kept ration tickets promising a week's grain, but the distributors withheld the food. When [PAWN_pronoun] refused to falsify the books, they expelled [PAWN_objective] from the office. All [PAWN_pronoun] took away was a small stack of tickets that could no longer be redeemed.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A038_GranaryRefuser.title: defiant granary guard
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A038_GranaryRefuser.descrip: [PAWN_nameDef] was hired to guard a granary, expecting to keep outside thieves away. Instead, the owner secretly removed the grain and locked hungry people inside. [PAWN_pronoun] refused to keep watch and became a refugee alongside the abandoned guards.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A039_HomeboundDeserter.desc: [PAWN_nameDef] was drafted into a unit short of food, while the officer kept the last sack of grain. During a retreat, [PAWN_pronoun] abandoned [PAWN_possessive] weapon and went back to look for family. The unit branded [PAWN_objective] a deserter, and the home village was already empty.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A040_CampTrapSetter.title: camp trapper
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A040_CampTrapSetter.descrip: When the old camp fence failed to stop nightly attacks by animals and grain thieves, [PAWN_nameDef] set traps outside it. After the camp burned, [PAWN_pronoun] used the same trapcraft learned while hunting to protect [PAWN_objective] on the road.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A041_GrainThiefOutcast.desc: [PAWN_nameDef] joined a band of starving ratkin to seize grain. Once inside the warehouse, dividing the spoils quickly turned into infighting. [PAWN_pronoun] escaped, but other settlements treated [PAWN_objective] as a grain thief, forcing [PAWN_objective] to hide in the wasteland.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A042_ScarredHunter.title: scarred hunter
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A042_ScarredHunter.descript: [PAWN_nameDef] lived by hunting until drought depleted the game and nobles closed the woods. While tracking a wounded animal, [PAWN_pronoun] ran into a rat swarm, suffered scars, and lost [PAWN_possessive] home. [PAWN_pronoun] later joined refugees seeking new hunting grounds.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A043_GranaryRatcatcher.desc: [PAWN_nameDef] cleared rat holes at a granary, but when the rats multiplied the owner charged all the losses to the workers. On the night the grain was ruined, [PAWN_pronoun] was driven out of the village and had to take the ratcatching work to another camp.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A044_QuarantinePorter.title: quarantine hauler
hauler
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A044_QuarantinePorter.descr: With family confined to plague quarantine sheds, [PAWN_nameDef] hauled medicine and drinking water at the village gate. When the sick ward burned, [PAWN_pronoun] lost both the relatives and the settlement. The memory of those sheds remained after [PAWN_pronoun] left.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A045_QuarantineWatcher.desc: [PAWN_nameDef] guarded the quarantine shed at the village entrance and tried to separate fever patients from healthy people. Once medicine and grain ran out, the villagers blamed the guards. Forced to leave, [PAWN_pronoun] searched for somewhere willing to take the sick.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A046_PostPlagueCaretaker.de: [PAWN_nameDef] survived a plague lockdown, but the recovered received neither grain nor permission to go home. After the old lodging was burned to an empty lot, [PAWN_pronoun] left with companions still recovering and sought a shed where they could rest.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A047_DisguisedGrainThief.de: After the family went days without food, [PAWN_nameDef] slipped into a granary at night to steal grain. When the theft was discovered, companions handed [PAWN_objective] over in exchange for passage. During the flight that followed, [PAWN_pronoun] learned to pose as an ordinary refugee to get past checkpoints.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A048_SiegeTunnelDigger.desc: With grain raiders surrounding the camp and no help arriving, [PAWN_nameDef] and companions dug a narrow passage under the wall and led people out. Looking back, [PAWN_pronoun] saw the camp burning, along with the belongings left by the family.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A049_GranaryBreaker.title: granary-breaking carpenter
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A049_GranaryBreaker.descrip: [PAWN_nameDef] repaired doors for a living. During the famine, the granary stayed locked and its grain was left to spoil rather than feed the hungry. Hearing someone call for help inside, [PAWN_pronoun] broke the door open, then had to flee home to escape pursuit.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y001_RuinsLitter.title: child lost in the fire
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y001_RuinsLitter.descriptio: [PAWN_nameDef] was separated from [PAWN_possessive] mother when an arson fire broke out and hid in a collapsed house. A few days of scrap grain kept [PAWN_objective] alive, but the rescuers had gone. [PAWN_pronoun] eventually left with refugees who passed afterward.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y002_LostFieldLitter.title: displaced farm child
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y002_LostFieldLitter.descri: [PAWN_nameDef] grew up on a small farm. The owner sold the land and took the adult workers away, leaving children behind as the crops were requisitioned. [PAWN_pronoun] had to follow refugees in search of food.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y003_CreviceMessenger.title: cave child messenger
messenger
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y003_CreviceMessenger.descr: [PAWN_nameDef] lived in a cave settlement where adults split into groups over food. Small enough to squeeze through the cracks, [PAWN_pronoun] became their messenger. When smoke and rats made the caves unlivable, [PAWN_pronoun] followed the last group to the surface.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y004_GrainMillApprentice.de: [PAWN_nameDef] lived with [PAWN_possessive] mother beside a grain mill, where broken grain was the family's most reliable food. After the mill was requisitioned, even moldy grain went into the rations. Mother and child were driven out together.
As the adults in the group fell ill one after another, [PAWN_nameDef] had to look after younger ratkin. During a night march, the children followed [PAWN_objective], but all became separated from their relatives. Afterward, they followed whoever would share food.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y006_LandmarkRememberingOrp: Separated from family during an evacuation, [PAWN_nameDef] remembered dead trees, a cracked bridge, and dangerous crossings. [PAWN_pronoun] used those landmarks to avoid pursuit and was taken in by another refugee group, but never found the old home.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y007_LivestockApprentice.de: As a child, [PAWN_nameDef] drove the family's remaining livestock. The farm lost its water, then most of its animals were requisitioned. When the pens were abandoned, [PAWN_pronoun] caught up with the refugees with a few surviving animals and never returned.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y008_OrphanedMillApprentice: The adults left a mill in debt for grain, abandoning [PAWN_nameDef] beside a millstone too heavy to turn. [PAWN_pronoun] learned the simplest mill work there. When the mill was torn down, [PAWN_pronoun] left with those few skills.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y009_CampfireListener.title: campfire story listener
listener
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y009_CampfireListener.descr: [PAWN_nameDef] was born into a refugee column, had never seen a good harvest, and fell asleep to adults' stories of past crops. When the group broke up for lack of food, they left [PAWN_objective] beside the campfire. [PAWN_pronoun] moved on only when another band of refugees passed.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y010_QuarantineShedChild.de: [PAWN_nameDef] was confined to a quarantine shed with family. At first, people brought food and water through the door. As the plague worsened, the deliveries stopped and relatives left or died. When the shed was dismantled, [PAWN_pronoun] escaped with the survivors.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y011_RuinedHouseOrphan.desc: A night raid separated [PAWN_nameDef] from family. [PAWN_pronoun] hid in a ruined house and survived on roots and rainwater. The searchers never returned, and afterward [PAWN_pronoun] moved alone between refugee camps looking for a place to stay.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y012_NightWatchApprentice.d: The refugee camp was repeatedly raided, and the adults' watches could not stop grain thieves. Unable to sleep, [PAWN_nameDef] memorized the patrol routes. After one raid separated [PAWN_objective] from family, [PAWN_pronoun] kept watching the campfires for others.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A050_ElderSisterProtector.d: After the parents died on the refugee road, [PAWN_nameDef] was the only one left to care for the younger siblings in their small settlement. The column later left [PAWN_objective] and the children beside the road to lighten its load. As their older sister, [PAWN_pronoun] had to lead them in search of somewhere willing to take young ratkin.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A051_IllMotherLeavingA.desc: [PAWN_nameDef], a ratkin mother, fled a village overrun by plague with the children, surviving on broken grain and herbs. As the illness worsened, [PAWN_pronoun] knew the next camp was out of reach. [PAWN_pronoun] still got the children to a strange settlement's gate before collapsing.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A052_BeggingRatkinMother.de: [PAWN_nameDef], a ratkin mother, supported the children by washing clothes and tending livestock until famine struck and the employers took back the grain and wages. Unwilling to hand the children to roadside strangers, [PAWN_pronoun] went from door to door begging for food.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A053_GrainThiefForFamily.de: [PAWN_nameDef] guarded the family's last sack of grain, but the children still collapsed from hunger. With no one willing to spare food, [PAWN_pronoun] entered a storehouse at night. The theft was discovered before [PAWN_pronoun] could get far, and [PAWN_pronoun] eventually left with only the empty bowl the family had left behind.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A054_WastelandSurvivor.desc: Grain raiders scattered [PAWN_nameDef]'s settlement during the night. [PAWN_pronoun] woke with only torn clothes on an unfamiliar wasteland road. Unable to find family, [PAWN_pronoun] followed animal tracks and distant cooking smoke in search of living people.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A055_RefugeeCampSteward.des: [PAWN_nameDef] assigned sleeping places and drinking water in a refugee camp. More people kept arriving until food, firewood, and everyone's patience ran short. When the camp broke up, [PAWN_pronoun] had no home to return to and left with the last group seeking another settlement.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A056_CageWatcher.title: prisoner cage guard
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A056_CageWatcher.descriptio: [PAWN_nameDef] guarded cargo and prisoner cages for a caravan. When the trade route failed, the caged children became bargaining chips for grain. The leader abandoned the group, leaving [PAWN_objective] to take the surviving prisoners in search of someone willing to negotiate.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A057_RatEggMerchant.title: trader in young ratkin
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A057_RatEggMerchant.descrip: [PAWN_nameDef] once believed that selling children to people with grain would at least get them through winter. Neither side could provide what had been promised. [PAWN_pronoun] had to walk on with a line of silent young ratkin, growing less able to look them in the face.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A058_OutwallBeggar.title: beggar outside the walls
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A058_OutwallBeggar.descript: [PAWN_nameDef] and other refugees built shelters outside an abandoned wall, hoping to avoid the fighting by staying out of the city. Once the gates closed, they had neither a route back nor food. [PAWN_pronoun] went on to beg repeatedly around the next settlement.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A059_ReliefKitchenCook.desc: [PAWN_nameDef] cooked the refugee column's grain from different sources in a single pot, until even the pot was traded for firewood. When a relief group arrived, all [PAWN_pronoun] had to offer were recipes and experience sorting out moldy grain. [PAWN_pronoun] wanted everyone to share the meal.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A060_RefugeeMedic.title: refugee medic
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A060_RefugeeMedic.descripti: [PAWN_nameDef] carried herbs in a small clinic. After it closed, medicine became the refugee group's most fought-over possession. [PAWN_pronoun] hid the last doses in [PAWN_possessive] clothes and brought feverish companions to a colony's edge to ask for help.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A061_SilverTrader.title: silver-carrying trader
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A061_SilverTrader.descripti: [PAWN_nameDef] sold the household tools, livestock, and house deed for silver, expecting money to buy safe passage. Checkpoint fees kept rising and the caravans changed their routes. With enough silver for only another stretch, [PAWN_pronoun] sought a settlement willing to trade.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A062_FragmentMapInformant.d: [PAWN_nameDef] obtained half a treasure map from a dead informant beside the road, but its locations were incomplete. [PAWN_pronoun] brought the fragment to a colony to trade for grain, medicine, or silver for the onward journey.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A063_RuinInformant.title: ruins informant
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A063_RuinInformant.descript: [PAWN_nameDef] hid in buildings hollowed out by rats and heavy rain, memorizing the usable doors, wells, and basements. The companions turned on one another over the map. [PAWN_pronoun] escaped with incomplete locations, hoping to exchange the information for safe passage.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A064_SmallSettlementClerk.d: [PAWN_nameDef] kept records in a small settlement that maintained order until someone altered the granary accounts. When its people split over the grain, [PAWN_pronoun] fled with the location of another small settlement, hoping to trade it for supplies that could be carried away.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A065_PregnantRefugee.title: pregnant refugee
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A065_PregnantRefugee.descri: [PAWN_nameDef] traveled pregnant with a group seeking shelter from the rain, but camps admitted only people ready to work. Disease or a fight over grain scattered the group. Near childbirth, [PAWN_pronoun] went to an unfamiliar colony to ask for a corner to stay in.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A066_MisdeliveredCargoCarri: [PAWN_nameDef] checked manifests and hauled supplies for a transport crew until a coordinate error sent an entire shipment into empty wilderness. The sender fled first. [PAWN_pronoun] followed it to the wrong site, recovered a few items, and sought help from the intended colony.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A067_MisidentifiedKin.title: mistaken kin seeker
kin seeker
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A067_MisidentifiedKin.descr: [PAWN_nameDef] lost contact with family during a night evacuation. After hearing a description of a similar child, [PAWN_pronoun] mistook an unrelated child for kin. By the time the mistake was clear, the old group was far away, leaving [PAWN_objective] unable to keep the child or return home.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A068_FamineFarmer.title: famine farmer
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A068_FamineFarmer.descripti: [PAWN_nameDef] kept working the old fields, hoping another season would bring rain, but eventually lost even the seed. Grain levies came one after another, and relatives died of plague. [PAWN_pronoun] divided the last food and left the village.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A069_AmbushedEscort.title: ambushed caravan escort
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A069_AmbushedEscort.descrip: [PAWN_nameDef] escorted medicine and grain for a caravan until desperate refugees blocked its path. The caravan fled, abandoning the cargo and the wounded. [PAWN_pronoun] crawled out of a stripped wagon and never trusted its banner again.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A070_PlaguezoneExile.title: plague zone exile
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A070_PlaguezoneExile.descri: [PAWN_nameDef]'s camp was declared a plague zone, barring its people from safe roads and clean food. Some collapsed; others were left behind. [PAWN_pronoun] led those still able to walk around the settlements and eventually reached an unfamiliar colony.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A071_QuarantineGatekeeper.d: [PAWN_nameDef] guarded the village quarantine shed, deciding each day who could enter, receive medicine, or remain outside. Once both medicine and grain ran out, patients and guards alike were expelled. [PAWN_pronoun] took the survivors in search of another shelter.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A072_PlagueCampTunnelDigger: [PAWN_nameDef] was trapped in a plague camp as hungry people and infected ratkin closed in. Those outside dared not open the gates, and there was no food inside. [PAWN_pronoun] dug a passage barely wide enough for one person beneath the wall and escaped, never learning whether those left behind survived.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A073_EscapedPlagueMessenger: [PAWN_nameDef] carried messages for a group of infected ratkin. They swore revenge on someone who had harmed them, but could not verify even a name. When revenge became their only concern, [PAWN_pronoun] fled with the letter that had no recipient.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A074_EvacuationGuide.title: evacuation guide
LanguageData.RHAH_History_A074_EvacuationGuide.descri: [PAWN_nameDef] repaired wooden huts and distributed drinking water in a temporary refugee camp until a neighboring power gave them days to leave. Before the attack, [PAWN_pronoun] led those able to walk out through the back gate. Looking back, [PAWN_pronoun] saw the huts [PAWN_pronoun] had built burning.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y013_CrowdBornChild.title: crowd-separated child
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y013_CrowdBornChild.descrip: [PAWN_nameDef] was carried among a huge refugee column, where every halt pushed someone out of the line. After a scramble for grain, [PAWN_pronoun] remembered only the family's voices and was taken away by another group.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y014_AbandonedHouseRatEgg.d: [PAWN_nameDef], a young ratkin, was left behind the door of an empty house with one hardened piece of food. The adults promised to return soon, but footsteps outside grew fewer. Only when passing refugees found [PAWN_objective] did [PAWN_pronoun] leave the house.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y015_DoorstepRatEgg.title: doorstep young ratkin
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y015_DoorstepRatEgg.descrip: Feverish, [PAWN_nameDef] was carried to a strange settlement's gate by [PAWN_possessive] ratkin mother, whose repeated touch on [PAWN_possessive] brow was all [PAWN_pronoun] remembered. Too weak to go farther, the mother pushed [PAWN_objective] inside and stayed outside. It was [PAWN_possessive] earliest memory.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y016_RationingApprentice.de: As the adults in a begging group dwindled, [PAWN_nameDef] was assigned to remember who had already received a spoonful of food. When there was not enough to share, [PAWN_pronoun] gave the last portion to a younger ratkin and was expelled from the group.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y017_GrainBarrelHiddenChild: The family brought [PAWN_nameDef] into a storehouse to steal grain. When the plan failed, the adults fled without looking back for [PAWN_objective]. [PAWN_pronoun] hid in an empty grain barrel until dawn, and afterward always checked for an escape route before trusting companions.
As a child, [PAWN_nameDef] lived with ratkin in a wasteland cave. Heavy rain flooded the entrance, and the adults left first with those able to walk. [PAWN_pronoun] hid among bushes and ruins for days before a passing group heard [PAWN_objective] crying.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y019_ChildByTheCage.title: child beside the cages
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y019_ChildByTheCage.descrip: [PAWN_nameDef] grew up beside merchant wagons, watching medicine, grain sacks, and young ratkin locked in separate cages. When the trade route failed, the leader abandoned both cargo and children. [PAWN_pronoun] had to follow the guard in search of a new trading stop.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y020_HiddenTradeChild.title: child hidden under a wagon
hidden child
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y020_HiddenTradeChild.descr: [PAWN_nameDef] listened to adults discussing grain prices and who could take the children, unaware that [PAWN_pronoun] was being traded too. When the deal failed, [PAWN_pronoun] was hidden beneath a wagon and left the camp with the merchant and the other young ratkin.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y021_SiegeCampWaterRunner.d: [PAWN_nameDef] was trapped in a besieged camp where water could be fetched only through a narrow gap along the wall. Small enough to fit, [PAWN_pronoun] was sent to carry half-bowls to the gate guards and younger children. When the wall fell, [PAWN_pronoun] left with those who escaped.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y022_ReliefLedgerChild.desc: [PAWN_nameDef] tracked each batch of supplies at a relief camp, including who received food but never got medicine. When the relief group left, [PAWN_pronoun] copied the remaining sack counts and names onto a piece of wood and traveled on with the incomplete list.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y023_MapLostChild.title: lost map-following child
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y023_MapLostChild.descripti: [PAWN_nameDef] followed an informant past treasures, ruins, and small settlements marked on a map, assuming every circle meant somewhere to sleep. After a deal failed, the informant fled alone. [PAWN_pronoun] was left with only a few vague landmarks.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y024_BirthConvoyChild.title: child separated from mother
lost child
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y024_BirthConvoyChild.descr: [PAWN_nameDef] traveled at the rear of a column with [PAWN_possessive] mother, who was close to giving birth. Every stop began with a search for shelter from the wind. The adults split mother and child between groups because of disease and scarce food, and [PAWN_pronoun] reached a colony's edge holding the mother's empty bag.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y025_MisdeliveredChild.desc: [PAWN_nameDef] was supposed to travel with supplies to an agreed camp, but woke beside a transport crate at the wrong destination. The haulers noticed the bad coordinates and left first. [PAWN_pronoun] waited among the unfamiliar cargo until refugees took [PAWN_objective] away.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y026_MisnamedChild.title: misnamed child
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y026_MisnamedChild.descript: During an evacuation, someone called [PAWN_nameDef] by another child's name. Afraid of being left behind, [PAWN_pronoun] did not correct it. The real family never came, and the mistaken guardian left after a quarrel, leaving [PAWN_objective] to search for a group under the unfamiliar name.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y027_FamineCampChild.title: child without a harvest
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y027_FamineCampChild.descri: The first field [PAWN_nameDef] saw had already been emptied by grain collectors. The adults kept promising the next season, but it brought only moldy seeds and sick people. The family split up while rations were distributed, and [PAWN_pronoun] left with refugees without ever seeing a real harvest.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y028_PlaguezoneChild.title: plague zone child
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y028_PlaguezoneChild.descri: [PAWN_nameDef] and family were expelled from a plague zone and had to wait outside each settlement for inspection. Fewer people brought food, and relatives gradually became unable to walk. [PAWN_pronoun] carried an empty medicine bag and an unfinished list of names toward the next quarantine shed.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y029_WoodenShelterOrphan.de: [PAWN_nameDef] grew up in a refugee camp's wooden huts, knowing which doors let in drafts and which wells still held water. When the camp was ordered to leave, adults divided the children between groups. [PAWN_pronoun] lost the family during the night and took away only a board with carved marks.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y030_DroughtFieldApprentice: [PAWN_nameDef]'s family fields failed for two seasons, and the adults saved the last water for seed. The child spent each day along the ridges gathering windblown ears of grain. The dry fields were abandoned in the end, and [PAWN_pronoun] left with the refugees.
[PAWN_nameDef]'s family collected seed for a grain mill. Damp in the warehouse mixed sound seed with moldy grain, and [PAWN_pronoun] learned to tell them apart while sorting sack after sack with the adults. When the mill closed, that knowledge was all that remained.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y032_FenceHerdingChild.desc: When a farm dismissed its workers, [PAWN_nameDef] was left in the pens with a few animals that had not been requisitioned. Once the water supply failed, [PAWN_pronoun] drove them after a refugee column. No one returned to the farm afterward.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y033_DryWellWaterChild.desc: The village well dried up in late summer, and adults barred their doors in a standoff over a bucket of water. Small enough to squeeze down a distant well that was nearly dry, [PAWN_nameDef] could still fetch water. When the village was abandoned, [PAWN_pronoun] left with the water crew.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y034_GrainSackRecorder.desc: [PAWN_nameDef] often waited at the granary door for family to finish work, eventually learning every kind of sack marking. The owner moved the stored grain and locked the doors. [PAWN_pronoun] left remembering those marks, but never found the original granary again.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y035_MillhandHelperChild.de: [PAWN_nameDef] cleared chaff for the adults at a grain mill and ate the broken grain left over. After the mill was requisitioned, spoiled grain was forced into the rations. [PAWN_pronoun] and the family left before the food was distributed.
[PAWN_nameDef] helped a carpenter repair refugee carts as spokes broke one after another in the mud. A flood scattered the group, and the family never came. [PAWN_pronoun] had to leave with the next cart that could still roll.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y037_NeedleworkApprentice.d: After the family weaving shop closed, the adults cut old clothes into strips and [PAWN_nameDef] learned to thread needles and make repairs. A fire destroyed the last fabric. By the time [PAWN_pronoun] left with the refugees, those stitches were well remembered.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y038_HuntingGroundHelper.de: [PAWN_nameDef] followed family along the edge of a closed hunting ground, looking for wounded animals to trade for meat. A hunt ran into a swarm of rats, and the hunters never returned. [PAWN_pronoun] joined a refugee column with the remaining hides.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y039_HerbBasketApprentice.d: When an herbalist fell ill, [PAWN_nameDef] carried the herb basket between quarantine sheds and homes. The herbalist died, and the shed doors were sealed. [PAWN_pronoun] left with the survivors, still remembering which herbs could temporarily ease a fever.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y040_KilnsideChildWorker.de: [PAWN_nameDef] worked with family at a brick kiln, picking up cinders and hauling broken bricks beside the furnace. The owner withheld wages and closed the lodging. Once the fire went out, [PAWN_pronoun] had to seek another shelter with the kiln workers.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y041_CampfireOrphan.title: campfire kin seeker
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y041_CampfireOrphan.descrip: [PAWN_nameDef] lost the family in a crowd collecting rations. Remembering only the campfire they had tended, [PAWN_pronoun] followed fires at night for days. The search found no one, and [PAWN_pronoun] eventually left with people willing to share grain.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y042_RiverRaftApprentice.de: After a storm, [PAWN_nameDef] was left on a riverbank and built a raft from driftwood and old doors with a few other children. It carried [PAWN_objective] to an unfamiliar shore. Flood and famine had already destroyed the old village.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y043_RaidedVillageChild.des: [PAWN_nameDef] returned with family to a raided village to recover pots, cloth, and old blankets. Empty houses and rats filled the lanes, and when the family left again, they left [PAWN_objective] behind. [PAWN_pronoun] eventually escaped with the next group of searchers.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y044_SnowprintApprentice.de: After snow closed the mountain roads, [PAWN_nameDef] followed footprints toward the next campfire. An avalanche buried the old path, and a caravan later found [PAWN_objective]. Traveling with them, [PAWN_pronoun] began learning to read wind direction and tracks.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y045_PackAnimalApprentice.d: After thieves took the caravan's waterskins, [PAWN_nameDef] was assigned to lead the last pack animals into the shade. The caravan broke up, but no one came back for the child. [PAWN_pronoun] had to take the animals across the dry country with another refugee group.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y046_NightWatchChild.title: sleepless camp child
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y046_NightWatchChild.descri: Grain was stolen night after night from the refugee camp, despite the adults taking turns on watch. [PAWN_nameDef] could not sleep and learned to recognize all kinds of footsteps. After the camp moved, [PAWN_pronoun] still listened for steps in the night.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Y047_CheckpointEvasionAppre: [PAWN_nameDef] hid under carts with family to evade grain-tax checkpoints, gradually memorizing the patrol hours. At one inspection, the family was detained. [PAWN_pronoun] escaped into another group but never saw them arrive.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Newborn.title: famine-born child
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Newborn.description: [PAWN_nameDef] was born into a ratkin settlement already suffering famine. Before [PAWN_pronoun] was old enough to help with work, life on the road had already begun.
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Refugee.title: famine refugee
LanguageData.RHAH_History_Refugee.description: [PAWN_nameDef] left the ratkin settlement after the storehouse ran empty. Elsewhere, [PAWN_pronoun] still had to find work to pay for the next meal.
